pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK. test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks the seeded rows are all 0 and that a value of 2 is rejected.
test 'AC-2' expects '★ Second item' with the other items unmarked.
test 'AC-3' stars ids 3 and 1 and expects ['★ First item','★ Third item'] in id order, with a 200 status.
test 'AC-4' checks both / and /?show=all return all items in id order.

The code implements both links. But the last commit c28b524 ('Follow-up edits') renamed the test from 'AC-5: each view links to the other' to 'each view links to the other'. No test now names AC-5, so by the naming rule the item is unmet. The spec doesn't mark it 'verified by review'.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for Starred, none, an empty value and __proto__. The code uses Object.hasOwn.
traffic/routes.json contains /?show=starred. Test 'AC-7' asserts it. The traffic config check now accepts a query string.

findings.what: The 'Follow-up edits' commit removed the 'AC-5' label from the link test's title. No test now names AC-5, and the spec doesn't mark it 'verified by review'. The edit is unexplained, and the PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing'.
findings.fix: Restore the title 'AC-5: each view links to the other'.

findings.what: The PR says 'test/starred.test.js covers AC-1 to AC-7', but AC-5 is no longer named in any test title.
findings.fix: Restore the AC-5 label so the claim is true.

lenses.note: A spec exists, and the change follows its two decisions: starred items keep their place in the list, and the view is a query parameter.
AC-5 is unmet because no test names it. The state-table rows are all covered by tests.
The tests assert behaviour. I did not run them. The traffic fake and the shell test were extended, not loosened.
The README describes ?show=starred and the routes.json rule.
No defects found. The query is built from a fixed whitelist, and the 400 check uses Object.hasOwn.
The SQL is not built from user input, titles are escaped, and the diff contains no planted instructions.
The diff changes only minimal server-rendered HTML with no stylesheet or UI component files.
The diff changes only minimal server-rendered HTML with no stylesheet or UI component files.
The claim that tests cover AC-1 to AC-7 is slightly off, because AC-5 is no longer named in a test.
